_doc: Windsor connections probe - the ONE place that says which Windsor accounts we depend on,
which client each belongs to, whether a dashboard actually reads it, and when each connector
was last re-authorised. probe.py reads this; the Grid's Connections tab renders the result.
Per account: id (as the LOADER stores it, prefix-free), name, client (registry key), label,
expected = daily | ended | standby | retired | snapshot, alerts = whether a bad state EMAILS
(false for accounts no dashboard reads - they still show on the tab, they just cannot page us).
Per datasource: grant.last_reauth (the day the connector was last re-authorised in Windsor),
grant.reauth_by, grant.token_lifetime_days (the platform's TYPICAL lifetime; Windsor exposes no
expiry, so expiry_estimate = last_reauth + lifetime and the UI labels it an estimate).
last_reauth is the SEED only: the probe OBSERVES re-grants itself (Windsor's ds-accounts list gaining ids, or an
account flipping not_granted -> granted) and uses the later of the two dates. Edit it only to correct history.
_recipients_doc: The DEPLOYED list (Jerome's call, 2026-09-04): Jerome, Ian and Charles. Calvin (calvin@100.digital) is deliberately held back until the alerts have proven themselves - add the address here and redeploy, nothing else changes. For a LOCAL test send, do NOT edit this list: pass `--to jerome@bidbrain.ai` on probe.py, which overrides recipients for that one run. Editing the list to test it is how a test list gets deployed by accident. Read at send time from cfg['recipients'] and published into the payload, so the Grid tab always states the live list.

datasources.label: Google Ads (native BigQuery transfer)
_doc: NOT a Windsor connector - Google runs these, so there is nothing to probe and freshness is
the only signal. That is also why they belong here: a broken transfer leaves no Windsor
grant to fail, so the connector half of this monitor cannot see it at all.
table: use CampaignBasicStats, NEVER CampaignStats - the latter is also segmented by
click_type and DOUBLE-COUNTS impressions (22,892 vs a true 21,008 over one week). Clicks
agree, which is what makes it silent. See md/AGENTS.md.
date_expr: segments_date, NEVER __TABLES__.last_modified. A DTS run that loads nothing
still TOUCHES the table, so last_modified advances straight through an outage and reports
green - exactly how the MCC failure of 2026-08-18 stayed invisible.
All five verified fresh 2026-09-04 (max segments_date 2026-09-02/03). md/AGENTS.md said TLM
and Reset Data were still frozen on the MCC set; that is stale - both have their own
per-account transfer since 2026-08-25 (GADS_LIVE_FROM in ingest/dts_data_pull/create_views.py).

grant.note: Native DTS, authorised by the Google account that owns the transfer. No token to expire, but it DOES break when upstream access is revoked - which is what freshness catches.

datasources.label: GA4 (native BigQuery transfer)
_doc: date_expr is _PARTITIONTIME because the p_ga4_* tables carry NO date column at all -
16 columns, not one of them a date - so the ingestion partition is the only per-row time
that exists. Verified 2026-09-04.
NINE of these transfers are FAILING, all with 'User does not have permission to access the
Google Analytics property' - ian@100.digital was never granted GA4 Viewer on them. Eight
have no table at all, which is why classify() treats a missing table as a finding rather
than staying silent: a pure freshness check cannot see a feed that never existed.
Property -> client names come from PROPERTY_NAMES in ingest/dts_data_pull/create_views.py,
which is the authoritative map. STT and Reset Data read raw_ga4.perf_ga4 directly, so their
properties are on a live critical path and alert. The rest are marked standby with alerts
off - they are worth SEEING, not worth paging anyone about.

grant.note: Native DTS. Breaks on upstream GA4 property permission, not on a token.
